definition.name: THEY Choose Self-Preservation: The World's Cold Calculus to Cut Losses
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: At the world level the dilemma is priced as tactical arithmetic where self-preservation is the rational answer. When Morpheus is taken, Smith escalates to a doubled serum dosage that drives his alpha pattern into an ordered wave — the sign he is about to break (ev-031 sc-144) — rendering him a lost asset whose codes will soon expire. The crew's own survival protocol therefore defaults to pulling Morpheus's plug and abandoning him rather than mounting a rescue, a procedure Neo must physically interrupt to stop (ev-032 sc-148). That same survival logic governs the ship when hunted: Morpheus immediately converts to preservation protocol, reading the Sentinels, giving the crew minutes, and ordering the EMP charged (ev-040 sc-185). Cause to effect: capture -> imminent breaking -> rational abandonment -> ship-wide preservation, making sacrifice appear illogical.

chain.why_in_plot: Opens the objective_story pricing: Morpheus is taken in the basement under grenade fire (sc-122-124), converting the leader into a time-limited liability whose Zion codes will soon expire, establishing the tactical arithmetic where cutting losses to preserve the crew is the rational self-preservation answer.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING places the crew exposed inside the Matrix on a hostile extraction; the basement flight through grenade fire and the catch-basin escape creates the separation where Morpheus is left to hold off Smith in Room 808 and is captured.

chain.why_in_plot: Prices the captured asset as lost: Smith's doubled serum dosage driving Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave (sc-144-145) signals imminent breaking, rendering his codes soon compromised and making abandonment the cold, rational self-preservation calculus at world level.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-026: The basement capture delivers Morpheus into Agent custody on the government building roof and executive office; only because he is held captive can Smith escalate to the doubled serum interrogation that produces the ordered wave.

chain.why_in_plot: Enacts the world's cold calculus as procedure: the crew defaults to pulling Morpheus's plug to cut losses and preserve Zion/crew (sc-148), treating rescue as illogical self-sacrifice that Neo must physically interrupt, proving self-preservation is the system's default.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: The ordered-wave sign that Morpheus is about to break and his codes will expire triggers the survival protocol; because he is priced as a lost asset, Tank takes hold of the plug to abandon him rather than mount a rescue.

chain.why_in_plot: Resolves the objective logic ship-wide: when Sentinels are detected, Morpheus immediately converts to preservation protocol — reading the hologram radar, giving five or six minutes, ordering the EMP charged (sc-185-186) — applying the same cut-losses self-preservation that priced Morpheus as expendable.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: The plug-pulling protocol that rationalized abandoning one to save many establishes the template Morpheus now applies to the whole ship; the same preservation logic that would sacrifice Morpheus now commands charging the EMP to save the hovercraft rather than risking all.

definition.name: I Choose Self-Sacrifice: Neo's Faith Wager Against Logic
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Neo resolves the dilemma from the inside by refusing its arithmetic altogether. Because Morpheus already pinned an Agent and ordered Trinity to get Neo out, choosing to give his own life so the others could escape (ev-025 sc-115), Neo carries a debt that makes self-preservation cost his emerging self-respect. When the crew moves to pull Morpheus's plug, Neo stops it and commits to going back in while explicitly denying he is the One (ev-032 sc-148) — so the rescue has no prophetic cover and is a pure wager on a man, something he cannot justify logically, only believe in. That same refusal carries forward when cornered in the subway and urged to run: he turns back from the escalator to face the hunter instead of fleeing (ev-038 sc-179). Cause to effect: witnessed sacrifice -> internalized debt -> illogical faith-wager -> consistent refusal to flee.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus pins the Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, choosing to give his own life so Neo escapes. Neo witnesses this self-sacrifice firsthand, creating an internal debt that makes future self-preservation cost his emerging self-respect and refuses the dilemma's arithmetic.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING establishes Neo as a self-preserving outsider; witnessing Morpheus deliberately trade his freedom for Neo's escape provides the first personal debt that reframes self-preservation as self-betrayal.

chain.why_in_plot: Smith doubling the serum until Morpheus's alpha pattern orders into a wave signals he will break. For Neo's interior dilemma this makes rescue tactically hopeless, so choosing to go anyway cannot be justified logically and can only be an illogical faith wager on a man.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: Because Morpheus sacrificed himself to save Neo (ev-025), his capture and imminent breaking under serum is not distant intel but Neo's debt coming due, making the cost of abandonment internal and immediate.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo physically stops Tank from pulling Morpheus's plug and commits to re-enter while explicitly denying he is the One. With no prophetic cover the rescue becomes pure self-sacrifice, a wager he cannot justify logically, only believe in, resolving the dilemma from the inside.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: The ordered wave showing Morpheus will break (ev-031) removes any logical odds of success, so Neo's decision to stop the plug pull is enabled only as an illogical faith wager that embraces hopelessness rather than calculating it.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo drops the helicopter, guns down Agents and leaps after the handcuffed falling Morpheus to catch him mid-air as Smith shoots. He enacts the faith wager physically, risking his own life to honor the debt rather than preserve himself.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: Neo's commitment to re-enter without claiming to be the One (ev-032) directly enables the helicopter assault and mid-air catch; the physical risk is the execution of the prior interior wager.

chain.why_in_plot: Alone before the dead escalator and urged by Trinity to run, Neo turns back to face the hunter and hardens into gunfighter calm. He repeats the refusal to flee, proving the earlier illogical wager has become an internalized stance for self-sacrifice over self-preservation.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-034: Having enacted the wager by leaping after Morpheus at lethal risk (ev-034), Neo has internalized sacrifice as identity, enabling him to refuse the offered escape at the escalator and turn to face the hunter instead of fleeing.

definition.name: YOU Model Self-Sacrifice: Morpheus's Living Argument for the Other
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus, as YOU, is the living challenge who embodies the sacrifice horn and presses Neo toward it. He first models it directly by pinning an Agent and ordering Trinity to get Neo out, giving his life so the others escape (ev-025 sc-115). Captured and drugged, he then spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than saving himself by breaking and betraying Zion (ev-031 sc-144), refusing self-preservation through betrayal. After Neo's illogical rescue succeeds, Morpheus reframes that wager as destiny, reinterpreting both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One (ev-035 sc-170). Cause to effect: enacted sacrifice -> endured torture without breaking -> retrospective validation as destiny, converting Neo's faith-wager into a worldview where a man is worth any risk.

chain.why_in_plot: As YOU, Morpheus establishes the ideological setup for sacrifice by recounting the Oracle's prophecy and declaring 'the search is over,' framing Neo as the One worth any risk and committing to guide him, making his later self-sacrifice legible as a deliberate model for Neo.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING leaves Neo recovered but spent asking if he can go back; Morpheus entering his dark room to reframe rescue as destiny and declare the search over creates the faith-premise that enables all later modeling of sacrifice.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus enacts the YOU sacrifice horn directly: bursting through to pin the Agent and ordering Trinity to get Neo out, he chooses to give his own life so the others escape, providing Neo the living example of risking self to save another.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-014: The prophecy faith from ev-014 that Neo is the One worth any risk enables this physical enactment; when Agents ambush Neo in the crawlspace, Morpheus's prior commitment converts belief into action, sacrificing himself for Neo's escape.

chain.why_in_plot: As the YOU living argument under pressure, Morpheus extends sacrifice from single act to endurance: drugged with doubled serum driving his alpha pattern toward breaking, he spends his last agency resisting cracking rather than saving himself by betraying Zion, refusing self-preservation through betrayal.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: Because ev-025's sacrifice left Morpheus captured while Neo and Trinity escaped, he is now held in the executive office where Smith can escalate to doubled serum, turning enacted sacrifice into a sustained test of refusing to break.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus completes the YOU argument by retrospectively validating sacrifice as destiny: cutting off Neo's report, he reinterprets both prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One, converting Neo's faith-wager into a worldview where a man is worth any risk.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: Because Morpheus endured torture without breaking in ev-031 until Neo's illogical rescue succeeded, he survives to the rooftop to reframe that wager; endurance preserves the model so he can convert enacted sacrifice into destiny narrative for Neo.

definition.name: WE Choose Each Other: Neo and Trinity's Loyalty Over Survival
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: The Neo–Trinity WE lives the dilemma as loyalty versus survival, overriding the world's cut-the-loss logic. Gutted by both Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial that he is not the One, Trinity converts grief into command and insists on directing the rescue on her terms, binding herself to Neo's wager (ev-032 sc-148). Their reciprocity is shown inside the exit when Neo breaks free of Trinity's embrace and sends her out first (ev-030 sc-142), protecting the bond even while escaping. When the crew gives Neo up after he is shot and the monitors flatline, Trinity refuses the survival verdict entirely: she takes hold of his body and kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life (ev-044 sc-209). Cause to effect: shared grief -> joint wager -> mutual protection -> refusal to let the other be sacrificed, making WE the force that defeats self-preservation.

chain.why_in_plot: Inside the TV repair shop Neo breaks free of Trinity's embrace and sends her out first when the phone rings (sc-142), enacting WE mutual protection that puts the other's survival before own escape, showing loyalty overriding self-preservation.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING establishes the Neo-Trinity WE bond; the imminent exit pressure in sc-142 forces that bond to enact as reciprocal protection rather than individual flight.

chain.why_in_plot: Smith's doubled serum drives Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave as he fights to keep his mind from cracking (sc-145), gutting Trinity and creating the shared grief WE must convert into joint action rather than cutting losses.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-030: The relief of waking safe on the Main Deck in sc-143 enabled by ev-030 makes the torture in sc-145 land as shared WE grief; without having survived together, there is no together to be gutted.

chain.why_in_plot: Trinity converts grief over Morpheus's condition and Neo's denial he is not the One into command and insists on directing the rescue on her terms (sc-148), binding WE to a joint wager that rejects self-preservation logic.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: The gutting ordered-wave torture in ev-031 sc-145 enables this conversion; Neo stopping the plug on Morpheus in sc-148 only becomes a WE wager when Trinity claims co-direction.

chain.why_in_plot: Ripped back to the hovercraft Trinity demands to be sent back to Neo trapped with Smith (sc-177), refusing to preserve herself while WE's other half remains in lethal danger, choosing loyalty over survival.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: The joint wager to re-enter the Matrix together in ev-032 sc-148 enables this refusal; because WE chose to go back as one, her forced extraction through the phone in sc-176 is experienced as abandonment she must undo.

chain.why_in_plot: After Smith shoots Neo three times and monitors flatline as the crew gives him up (sc-209-210), Trinity refuses the survival verdict, takes hold of his body and kisses him, and WE revives him, defeating self-preservation's logic to cut losses.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-037: Trinity's refusal to leave Neo trapped with Smith in the subway in sc-177 enables her final refusal in sc-209; the same WE loyalty that demanded to be sent back now refuses to accept flatline as final.

chain.why_in_plot: In the darkened hovercraft Trinity keeps vigil as Neo wakes at her voice and reaches for her while she weeps and kisses him (sc-223), confirming WE's loyalty endures beyond the survival logic that declared him lost.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-044: The kiss that jumps monitors back to life in ev-044 sc-209 enables this waking; without WE's revival, there is no vigil breaking in sc-223 where his eyes open at her voice.

definition.name: WE (Crew) Split the Dilemma: Cypher's Self-Preservation vs the Crew's Sacrifice
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: The crew as a group lives out both horns of the dilemma at once. Cypher embodies self-preservation to its logical end, first recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a mere body count by telling him five before him took on an Agent and died (ev-020 sc-073), retreating Neo toward caution, then completing the horn by murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, only struck down by the surviving Tank (ev-029 sc-137). Against him, the rest of the crew — Tank, Switch, Apoc, Dozer — pay the price of the sacrifice horn, and their earlier split while watching Neo's failed jump between doubters and believers (ev-016 sc-058) shows a community actively wrestling with whether faith in one man is worth dying for. Cause to effect: cynical accounting -> betrayal for survival -> lethal cost to believers -> visible communal division over self-preservation versus sacrifice.

chain.why_in_plot: Crew watches Neo's failed rooftop jump split between doubters and believers, making visible a society-level deliberation where the WE actively wrestles over whether faith in one man is worth dying for — the communal divide between self-preservation and sacrifice.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Opening training ritual in the Construct creates a public test of faith; Neo's fall forces the crew watching on the main deck to reveal their divided stance, establishing the WE's collective dilemma.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher embodies the WE's self-preservation horn by recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a body count — five before Neo took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing — then bargaining with Smith over steak to save himself.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: The visible split between doubters and believers after the failed jump gives Cypher social proof and personal justification to voice his cynical accounting to Neo and to seek Smith's self-preservation deal.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher converts cynical accounting into active betrayal for the WE, covertly connecting a phone and dropping it in the alley garbage can to deliver the crew to the Agents, moving self-preservation from talk to material endangerment of the collective.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-020: Having struck his bargain with Smith in the restaurant, Cypher must provide the traceable signal Smith demanded, so he plants the connected phone as the crew enters the Matrix for the Oracle.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher reaching the TV repair shop exit first and waking on the ship to draw a concealed rifle positions the self-preservation horn to execute its lethal cost against the believing crew, staging the WE's internal murder for survival.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-021: The planted phone enabled the Agents to trace and trap the crew, forcing a panicked emergency exit where Cypher slips through the window first and wakes ahead of the others to seize the rifle.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher completes self-preservation to its logical end for the WE by murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, until surviving Tank strikes him down — the horn's lethal price made manifest within the crew.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-028: Waking first with rifle after reaching the exit gives Cypher unopposed physical position to shoot Tank, lie about an accident on the phone, and then murder the jacked-in crewmates and hand over Morpheus.

chain.why_in_plot: Survivors wake to count the sacrifice horn's price — Dozer dead, Tank wounded, Apoc and Switch gone — confirming for the WE that the believers' commitment to the collective costs lives while self-preservation is stopped.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-029: Cypher's murders aboard the ship directly create the casualties Trinity and Tank confront upon waking in the repair shop and on the main deck, turning betrayal into counted communal loss.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo and Trinity live the sacrifice horn Cypher rejected on behalf of the WE, storming the government building under certain death to extract Morpheus, with Neo leaping to catch his handcuffed body mid-fall rather than fleeing to save themselves.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-029: Cypher's delivery of Morpheus to the Agents creates the captivity that can only be undone by deliberate suicidal rescue, forcing the remaining crew to enact the opposite horn of the dilemma.

chain.why_in_plot: Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar the crew watches together as Neo halts the Agents' volley and destroys Smith while Morpheus declares him the One — communal vindication that the believers' costly sacrifice outweighed Cypher's self-preservation for the WE.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-034: The successful sacrifice rescue preserves Morpheus and enables Neo's transformation to be witnessed collectively on the ship's screens, turning earlier divided watching into unified vindication of faith over self-preservation.
